subject: MSA / Order Form: Clarify monetary cap carve-out for IP indemnity
messages:
From: Susan Klein <susan.klein@acme-retail.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-retail.com>

Subject: Re: Draft MSA / Order Form – IP indemnity / cap question

Hi Lauren / team,

Thanks for the revised MSA. Our legal team flagged the indemnity section — specifically the carve-out to the liability cap for IP infringement. We need clarity on whether Redwood is proposing an unlimited liability for third-party IP infringement or a monetary carve-out with conditions.

Acme’s position is that the MSA should not leave IP exposure uncapped without mitigations. Two options Acme would accept: (1) a defined monetary floor/cap for IP indemnity backed by evidence of insurance or (2) a mutually agreeable escrow or remediation-only path that limits recoverable damages.

Can you confirm Redwood’s preferred approach and, if you insist on an uncapped indemnity for IP, provide:
- examples of prior claims handled (high level, redacted) or
- proof of relevant IP insurance (certificate) or
- willingness to use escrow or stipulated remediations as primary remedy.

We attached a redline with our suggested language (see MSA_redline_20261130.docx). Please respond with Redwood’s position so we can move to procurement approvals.

Best,
Susan Klein
VP Legal, Acme Retail

Quick legal POV and a suggested compromise — see attached redline (Suggested_IP_Carveout_Redline.docx). High level:

1) We should avoid an unlimited, uncapped indemnity where possible. Market practice for SaaS/inference platforms is either:
   - a defined monetary carve-out for IP indemnity (commonly 2–3x ARR or a fixed multiple) OR
   - an uncapped obligation limited to actual defense costs + direct damages but only where customer demonstrates a valid third-party claim and we retain rights to control defense/remediation.

2) Proposed Redwood position (commercially practical):
   - Offer a monetary cap of $5,000,000 for third-party IP infringement indemnity as a default; but allow an uncapped make-whole remedy for court-awarded royalties if (and only if) the claim satisfies narrow criteria: willful infringement, and we had prior knowledge (rare).
   - Require customer to provide either: (a) evidence of IP infringement insurance covering claims above the cap, or (b) agreement to an escrow of an agreed remediation fund for claims related to customer-specific embeddings or custom model training artifacts.

3) Operational checks:
   - Acceptable evidence: COI (certificate of insurance), policy cover page showing IP coverage, or signed escrow agreement.
   - Process: customer must deliver COI before the start of a production-level deployment or before the first paid invoice over $250k TCV; otherwise fallback is the monetary cap only.

If sales wants a smaller cap (e.g., $2M) for speed, fine — but that will increase our commercial exposure. I recommend $5M for enterprise customers with >$1M TCV.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Agree with Karthik but adding the commercial lens:

- Acme is strategic (potential Dedicated deal). I’d prefer to propose the $5M cap plus COI requirement. That should be acceptable to procurement and keeps the deal moving.
- If Acme pushes back, we can offer a phased approach: $2M cap during initial 6-month go-live (proof of concept), bump to $5M on annual renewal or once production SLA thresholds are met.
- Escrow is a non-starter for most customers unless we clearly define trigger events and release conditions — procurement hates open-ended escrow. Insurance (COI) is the cleanest ask.

Action: Lauren — can you send Acme the $5M + COI position with our suggested Docs/links for COI templates? I can own the commercial follow-up.

Cheers,
Marissa
Director of Sales, Enterprise

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Susan Klein <susan.klein@acme-retail.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA / Order Form – IP indemnity / cap question

Susan — thanks for the clear callout and for sharing Acme’s redline. After internal review we’d like to propose a compromise to keep procurement moving:

- Redwood will accept a monetary cap on third-party IP infringement indemnity set at $5,000,000.
- Separately, Redwood will agree to make whole court-ordered royalties only in the limited circumstance of adjudicated willful infringement where Redwood had actual prior knowledge (this is a narrow exception).
- As a condition of the $5M cap, Acme must provide either: (1) a certificate of insurance evidencing IP infringement coverage with limits at or above the $5M cap, or (2) a signed escrow agreement (we can provide a template) establishing a remediation fund. If Acme does not provide evidence prior to production go-live (or before invoices exceed $250k TCV), Redwood’s liability will be limited to the default monetary cap without the additional remedy.

Operational notes / next steps:
- Please upload COI to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeMSA.
- If you prefer escrow, indicate and we’ll circulate the escrow template and timeline.
- If Acme accepts the $5M + COI approach, we can finalize the MSA + Order Form and move to signatures this week.

If Acme wants to propose a counter (e.g., $2M cap or phased cap tied to go-live), we can review but $5M + COI is our preferred path for an enterprise Dedicated deployment.

Thanks — looking forward to your quick confirmation so Marissa can route procurement.

Best regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
